deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 154, Jan. 1984): Σ = (D_1,…,D_n) is an arrangement of n pseudolines in the projective plane X. π: X̃ → X is the 2-sheeted cover, a sphere in which each D_i lifts to a closed curve D̃_i. Grothendieck classifies the relative positions (p.r.) of an extra pseudoline D with respect to Σ:
- stable: D is generic;
- sub-stable: D passes through exactly one vertex of Σ;
- supersingular: D coincides with some D_i.
From these he builds a 2-dimensional cell complex, the 'surface de déploiement'. Its faces are the stable positions, its edges come from sub-stable positions, and its vertices from more degenerate ones.

The previous page gives five variants:
- X_0: the n supersingular positions are vertices of order 4n instead of 4, i.e. ramification points.
- X_1: each supersingular position becomes a 'supercritical' face F_i. It is attached by arcs of combinatorial length 1 to the 2(n−1) nearby sub-stable faces, with the stable faces wedged between them and touching F_i at a vertex.

This page continues with X_1.
1. In X_1 every vertex, including those on the supercritical faces, has order 4. The vertices on F_i correspond to the 2n_i oriented edges of D_i (n_i = number of vertices of Σ on D_i, so n_i = n−1 in the simple case).
2. He then counts the 'bouts libres' (free ends) created at F_i when Σ is stable (simple), split by the parity of n:
   - n even: each sub-stable face contributes 2 free ends, at the ends of its incidence edge, and each stable face touching F_i contributes 1. Total 2·2(n−1) + 2(n−1) = 6(n−1), 'un peu beaucoup', i.e. redundant.
   - n odd: each adjacent sub-stable face contributes 1 free end, at the midpoint of the common edge, and the stable faces contribute 0. Total 2(n−1), 'just what is needed' to describe (X,Σ) 'affinised' by D_i, i.e. the affine arrangement obtained by sending D_i to infinity.
3. Remedy for all parities: start from X_0 and replace each supercritical vertex s by a small supercritical disk F_s. Now in one parity the sub-stable faces each give 1 free end and the stable faces give 0; in the other parity the roles are swapped. Either way 2(n−1) free ends land on ∂F_s. The polygon they form matches the one attached to D̃_i, the lift of D_i to the sphere X̃.
4. Margin note (NB): to glue F_i to the adjacent sub-stable faces one must choose on D̃_i 'arcs of generatrices' of combinatorial length 1. These are arcs other than the cell edges cut out by the vertices, placed equidistant from the two antipodal points of D̃_i corresponding to s. The red/yellow figure shows a disk with pseudolines, two antipodal black points, and a dashed yellow arc of length 1.

Purpose: find a combinatorial surface model of the space of one-pseudoline extensions of Σ that has no redundant boundary and no ramification. This feeds the next page's discussion of local systems / parallel transport of the polygons Pol(D) and the 'défaut' of ramification at supersingular points.
errors: In the remedy paragraph the text says 'Dans le cas n impair … et c'est l'inverse si n est impair'. One occurrence must be 'pair'; it is a slip, the intent being that the contributions swap with parity.
Terminology drifts between 'supersingulière' (previous page) and 'supercritique' (this page) for the same objects.

The parity dependence is asserted, not proved. It depends on how the length-1 arcs are positioned relative to the 2(n−1) vertices of D̃_i (equidistance between consecutive transition axes). This is plausible from antipodal symmetry (n−1 points of D_i ↔ 2(n−1) points on D̃_i), but no argument is given here.

ideas.what: Cell-complex 'surface de déploiement' parametrising relative positions of an extra pseudoline with respect to an arrangement Σ (stable / sub-stable / supersingular strata)
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (space of single-element extensions); dual pseudoline arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (enlargement lemma, 1926); Goodman–Pollack; Sturmfels–Ziegler 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Mnëv–Ziegler

ideas.what: Blowing up the supersingular (coincident-line) points into faces / small disks to remove ramification (vertex order 4n → 4)
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up / resolution of the branch points of the extension complex; making a branched-cover cell structure into a genuine surface
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (standard technique; no specific credit in the oriented-matroid literature)

ideas.what: Counting free boundary ends near a supersingular face with an answer depending on the parity of n (6(n−1) vs 2(n−1))
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of the extension space near a degenerate (parallel) extension; link of an element in the arrangement

ideas.what: Working on the double cover X̃ (sphere), with D̃_i the lift of D_i, to define 'arcs of generatrices' of combinatorial length 1 equidistant from antipodal points
ideas.modern_name: Oriented (signed) setting: pseudo-great-circle arrangements on S², i.e. oriented matroids rather than unoriented matroids

ideas.what: Free ends at F_s encode the affine arrangement obtained by sending D_i to infinity ('affinisé par D_i')
ideas.modern_name: Affine pseudoline arrangement / contraction–deletion at an element; wiring diagram from a choice of line at infinity

missed.claim: In 1984 Grothendieck is explicitly constructing, as a combinatorial surface, the space of all pseudolines extending a given arrangement, and analysing its local structure at degenerate extensions. This is the rank-3 extension space later studied by Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993), where the rank-3 case is shown to behave like a 2-sphere. His notes appear to anticipate the 'extension space' viewpoint and add something absent from that literature: the ramification and resolution analysis at the coincident positions D = D_i, and the idea of local systems / parallel transport of Pol(D) over it.
missed.quote: Pour l'étude des "bouts libres" créés, supposant pour fixer les idées Σ stable, on trouve suivant la parité de n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A comparison could give explicit combinatorial surface models of rank-3 extension spaces with controlled ramification. It could also suggest a local-system / monodromy viewpoint on extension spaces, which is not standard in oriented matroid theory.

missed.claim: The parity-dependent excess of free ends (6(n−1) for n even) and the proposed small-disk replacement are not carried through on this page. The next page reports the resulting surfaces still have ramification defects and lack identifications.
missed.quote: Le cas n impair est satisfaisant, mais par ce cas pair tel quel, on n'y a dans redondance de bouts libres. Une façon de s'en tirer dans tous les cas…
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A uniform (parity-free) cell model of the extension surface near degenerate extensions remains an explicit, checkable combinatorial question.

deep.surprise_reason: These are technical working notes inside an unpublished project on pseudoline arrangements that predates the extension-space literature. The page itself is a local bookkeeping computation (free-end counts, blow-up of branch points). The broader programme is notable, but this page adds only details.
transcription_corrections: 'aux incidents faces supercritiques' should read 'aux faces supercritiques incidentes' ('incidentes' is inserted above the struck 'deux').
'n-uples, [?] des fosses [?]' is likely 'n-uples, de façon … voir exactement une description de (X,Σ) "affinisé" par D_i'.
In the remedy paragraph, the first 'Dans le cas n impair' / second 'si n est impair': one should be 'pair'. The image reads 'n impair' then 'n est impair', so the slip is Grothendieck's.
'chaque face stable incidente 1 bout [?]' likely reads '0 bout' or '1 bout' depending on parity; the image suggests 'A bout' with A corrected.
Margin: 'qu'on choisit de la genre combinatoire 1' should read 'qu'on choisit de longueur combinatoire 1'.
Margin: 'trouvé le p.v. D' is probably 'trouve la p.r. D' (position relative).
Last line: 'cas, [?] à celui obtenu pour D̃_i' is probably '…qu'ils forment est canoniquement [isomorphe] à celui obtenu pour D̃_i'.
